source.title: A Minimalist Example of Edge-of-Stability and Progressive Sharpening
source.authors: Li-Ming Liu; Zi-Xuan Zhang; S. Du; Tuo Zhao

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. Some equations and figure content are flattened, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes a minimalist two-layer regression network and reports a CIFAR-10 learning-rate sweep bearing on edge-of-stability training dynamics, using a different setup from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior results on edge of stability, but those cited results are not rows. The paper's own two-layer CIFAR-10 experiment measures steps to reduce MSE from 0.32 to 0.22, not classification error.
record.test_reason: The study proves and numerically demonstrates progressive sharpening, self-stabilization and falling loss in a width-one regression network, bearing on V5's full-batch edge-of-stability component through a different setting and theoretical method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish sharpening, self-stabilization and loss convergence for their specially initialized regression model with clipping on β1. They numerically demonstrate recurring EoS dynamics and report that larger learning rates can slow CIFAR-10 loss reduction. Their unclipped examples include both similar dynamics and abnormal, slow recovery.
record.recipe_differences: The main analysis uses a width-one linear network, population square loss, a prescribed initialization set, and clipping on one parameter; the CIFAR-10 experiment uses a two-layer MLP, MSE, and a learning-rate sweep. Neither is the wide-network setting in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the CIFAR-10 loss-reduction time; clipping on β1 affects whether some runs exhibit abnormal dynamics. Theorems 4.3 and 4.4 also use different initialization sets or phases.

fits_no_version.finding: The CIFAR-10 ReLU MLP takes approximately 5000 versus 11000 steps to reduce MSE from 0.32 to 0.22 at learning rates 0.1 versus 0.3; the reported optimum is approximately 0.12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within the tested EoS regime, increasing the learning rate can slow training-loss reduction.

record.problems: The main proof concerns a specially initialized, clipped width-one regression model. The CIFAR-10 result measures MSE loss-reduction time rather than classification error; the sweep is shown mainly as a figure and no uncertainty or controls are reported.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random or corrupted labels.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention by residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed and trainable depth.
Wide-network catapult recovery relative to the initial linearized-model stability limit; divergence at larger rates; divergence despite starting below the threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, including Fixup.

missing.what: A separate successful unclipped run: initialization in X(1/30), η = 1/30, and 15000 training steps, with falling loss and dynamics described as similar to the clipped findings.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Its restricted regression construction extends evidence for V5's EoS component; it does not directly test the wide-network catapult component. No verdict follows from the CIFAR-10 speed comparison alone.

versions.untested_parts: The CIFAR-10 experiment reports MSE training-loss reduction steps, not training classification error; no CIFAR-100 or corrupted-label result.
No teacher-student local-minimum or width comparison.

The main analyzed network is a width-one linear regression model with a prescribed initialization set and clipping; it does not test wide networks or the initial linearized-model stability limit. No long-run full-batch sharpness-threshold experiment matching Cohen et al. or divergence comparison matching Gilmer et al.

rows.subject: two-layer width-one linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on population square loss, with clipping on β1 and initialization in X(η).
rows.measure: Training loss and sharpness along the GD trajectory
rows.value: For any δ > 0 and ϵ > 0, eventually L(θ(t)) ≤ ϵ and S(θ(t)) ≤ (2+δ)/η.
rows.note: The theorem establishes convergence of this specified regression model, not classification error on a benchmark.
rows.check: The theorem proves eventual arbitrarily small loss and an asymptotic sharpness upper bound; that bound alone does not establish hovering at the threshold. The operation clips the parameter update on β1, rather than applying ordinary gradient clipping.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Section 4 analysis assumptions; Theorem 4.1, equation (4.1).

rows.subject: two-layer width-one linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from X(η), with clipping on β1.
rows.value: α increases monotonically; sharpness is between 1.1/η and 1.7/η.
rows.note: The result describes sharpening below the 2/η threshold during this phase.
rows.check: This row covers only the preliminary sharpening phase below the threshold; it is not evidence that the later EoS effect fails. Theorem 4.3 also bounds sharpness between 1.5/η and 4.71/η after T1.

rows.subject: two-layer width-one linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from the more stable initialization subset X̃(η), with clipping on β1.

conditions.value: EoS phases identified by T2 and T3

rows.measure: Sharpness and α during progressive sharpening and self-stabilization
rows.value: At T2, S(θ(T2)) > 2.37/η; at T3, S(θ(T3)) < 2/η + η; α increases through T2 and decreases from T2 to T3.
rows.note: The theorem reports both crossing above the threshold and subsequent self-stabilization.
rows.check: The numerical bounds are correct. The T3 bound is 2/η + η, which does not strictly establish crossing below 2/η. Monotonicity is proved for α; sharpness is controlled through bounds involving α.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, definition of the stronger initialization subset and Theorem 4.4.

rows.subject: two-layer width-one linear network
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with η = 1/20 for 10000 iterations.
rows.note: The text says loss decreases over long timescales with periodic spikes, while sharpness grows and oscillates around 2/η.
rows.check: The accompanying text establishes declining loss over long timescales with periodic spikes and sharpness oscillating around 2/η = 40. Include clipping on β1 and initialization in X(η) in the conditions.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Gradient Descent learning-rate sweep; measured steps to reduce MSE training loss from 0.32 to 0.22.

conditions.value: first 10,000 CIFAR-10 images, without image preprocessing

rows.measure: Steps to reduce training loss from 0.32 to 0.22
rows.value: learning rate 0.3: 11000 steps; optimal learning rate approximately 0.12
rows.note: The paper says increasing the learning rate from 0.1 to 0.3 slows this loss reduction by about 50%. Figure 6 reports other rates graphically.
rows.check: Loss-reduction time across learning rates does not measure recovery across a stability threshold or sharpness hovering. V5 does not assert that larger rates always accelerate training. The reported 5000 versus 11000 steps means 120% more steps, inconsistent with the paper's stated 50% slowdown.

rows.subject: two-layer network in the paper's setting
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent without clipping on β1.
rows.value: In some cases dynamics deviate from EoS and exhibit abnormal behavior; α can become very small, gradients become negligible, and recovery is extremely slow.
rows.locator: Appendix F, Figure 14 and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper also says not all unclipped runs become poorly behaved; it gives an η = 1/30, 15,000-step run as similar to the clipped findings (Figure 13).
rows.check: The unclipped example shows sharpness collapsing and extremely slow recovery, rather than sustained EoS behavior. It does not establish divergence or failure of eventual convergence. Separate the successful η = 1/30 run from this abnormal η = 1/20 condition.
